headline: The hard-cap source-aware retrieval isolation form failed and should not be kept active, but the attributable regression is narrower than the raw 5/10 total.

gpt4_d6585ce8.summary: Selective without isolation presented 12 facts and was correct; hard-cap isolation presented 7 facts and was wrong. The failure is attributable to context starvation from shrinking below max_facts.

195a1a1b.summary: Both selective and isolation had 8 retrieved facts and neither had lexical gold in top-k; the selective run happened to pass while isolation did not.

interpretation_caveats: The experiment conflated source-aware reordering with hard-capping assistant facts below max_facts.
The evidence disproves the hard-cap truncation form, not all source-aware ordering.
The regression magnitude is based on a single n=10 servicebus run; treat the direction as useful but not a precise stable effect.
The breadth signal remains the main root-cause evidence: 488 assistant turns extracted and only 36 skipped.
recommended_next_slice: Revert the hard-cap runtime isolation commit.
Prioritize a genuinely stricter assistant extraction gate before more retrieval isolation.
If testing retrieval isolation again, use a soft-reorder/fill-to-max variant or assistant-facts-as-fallback-only so context is not starved.
Preserve the 488/36 breadth number as the before metric for the next extraction-gate slice.
